page: Amazon Web Services r8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors on the arm64 architecture. The server provides 192 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by 1536 GB of DDR5 system memory. Cache hierarchy includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. It incorporates a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance features no local NVMe storage, relying completely on external network-attached volumes, and contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional multi-core and memory throughput. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-threaded CPU stress testing, Clang software compilation, and PassMark database operations. In-memory data store evaluations record 357.86 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, reinforced by large-block memory read bandwidth approaching 896.26 GB/s and write bandwidth exceeding 412.85 GB/s. Static web serving throughput also places in the top decile. Conversely, single-thread performance on Geekbench and stress-ng falls within the median range.

Hardware tradeoffs include the absence of onboard NVMe drives and x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX-512 or AMX. Large language model text generation throughput remains weak compared to accelerator-backed nodes, although prompt processing performs moderately well across medium and large models. The architecture provides high resource density per socket with an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, delivering cost efficiency for heavily parallelized, memory-bound enterprise systems.

Amazon Web Services r8g.metal-48xl is best suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis, enterprise database management systems, extensive Clang build farms, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance featuring 192 physical arm64 cores powered by AWS Neoverse-V2 Graviton processors running at 2.7 GHz. Configured with 1536 GB of DDR5 memory, it provides an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. The hardware profile includes 50 Gbps baseline networking, zero discrete GPUs, and no bundled local storage. In benchmark testing, the server exhibits top-tier multi-threaded execution, high memory read and write bandwidth, and outstanding throughput in Redis operations, software compilation, and database processing. Single-core performance registers in the median range, and text generation efficiency is constrained by the lack of dedicated vector or matrix hardware accelerators. The platform offers efficient resource density for massive in-memory databases, distributed caching clusters, parallel compilation farms, and high-throughput web serving environments.
